gaps.sentence: By the time you read this, the treaty ___ (sign) by all twelve delegations.
gaps.explanation: 'By the time + present clause' with a future meaning takes the future perfect passive.

gaps.sentence: My laptop ___ (service) next week, so back up your files beforehand.
gaps.explanation: 'Next week' takes the future passive: will be + serviced (is being serviced is also a valid arrangement).

gaps.sentence: She had her laptop ___ (repair) after the coffee spill.
gaps.explanation: Causative structure: had + her laptop + repaired. A technician performed the repair.

gaps.sentence: The divers ___ (know) to have been working without insurance.
gaps.explanation: are known to have been working: the knowing is present, the working was ongoing before.

gaps.sentence: The bridge ___ (inspect) twice a year for signs of corrosion.
gaps.explanation: 'Twice a year' marks a routine: present simple passive, is + inspected.

gaps.sentence: We had the whole house ___ (repaint) before the wedding.
gaps.explanation: 'Had the house repainted' — painters did it at our request. Object + past participle.

gaps.sentence: The castle ___ in the twelfth century.
gaps.explanation: A completed past date takes the past simple passive.

gaps.sentence: Over two hundred bird species ___ (record) in the valley this spring.
gaps.explanation: 'This spring' is an open time frame, so present perfect passive: have been + recorded.
